\[
E(A) = \lambda \sum_p R_p(A_p) + \sum_{\{p,q\},\ A_p \ne A_q} B_{pq},
\qquad
B_{pq} = \exp\left(-\frac{(I_p - I_q)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right) \frac{1}{\operatorname{dist}(p,q)}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(A_p\): The label of pixel p, object or background
- \(R_p\): The region cost of the label at p
- \(B_{pq}\): The boundary cost between neighbors p and q
- \(\lambda\): The region weight
- \(\sigma\): The edge contrast

A labels every pixel p as object or background. The region term R is the cost of the label at p. It is minus the log of how likely the brightness I at p is among the seeds of that label. The boundary term B is the cost of cutting between neighbors p and q. It is high when they look alike. Boykov and Jolly built a graph with one node per pixel and two terminals. The source stands for the object, the sink for the background. Neighbor links carry B. Each unknown pixel links to the source with lambda R(background) and to the sink with lambda R(object). A seed links to its own terminal with a weight K. K is larger than any cut through its neighbors, so a seed never changes side. A minimum cut of this graph is a minimum of E, and a maximum flow finds it.
